purpose: Bounded Fair Work Commission case linking long-term platform work, complaint-triggered deactivation, alternative earnings, a defined lost-earnings calculation, and an ordered monetary remedy without treating the order as receipt.

events.geography: Australia; Fair Work Commission UDE2025/141, Uber Driver Platform
events.date_precision: deactivation on 13 June 2025; decision and order dated 17 October 2025; reactivation ordered within 7 days
events.denominator: One publicly adjudicated platform worker case; no population denominator
events.method: Structured extraction from the primary Fair Work Commission decision [2025] FWC 3111
events.missingness: Worker household records, exact payment execution, post-order account activity, later earnings, health, trust, recurrence, and exit are not retained
events.exposure: A driver who had worked through the Uber Driver Platform since February 2016 was deactivated after a 2025 rider complaint and older complaints were treated as a pattern, despite the Commission finding the evidence insufficient for a valid reason
events.alternatives_before_action: The public record does not identify feasible alternatives before deactivation; after deactivation the worker earned $9,000 from Baysec and increased Didi earnings, which were treated as substitute earnings in the remedy calculation
events.immediate_burden_or_benefit: The worker lost his primary platform income and reported severe financial hardship, distress, humiliation, and reputational damage; the Commission calculated lost earnings before substitute-earnings deductions
events.choice_or_response: The worker responded to the preliminary notice, requested a discussion, gave evidence, and pursued the unfair-deactivation remedy route
events.person_or_actor_with_control: Uber controlled platform access and complaint processing; riders supplied complaints; the worker controlled response and application; the Commission controlled the remedy and lost-earnings calculation
events.remedy_or_institutional_response: The Commission found deactivation unfair, ordered reactivation on the same terms within 7 days, and ordered $6,073.23 gross less tax for lost earnings within 14 days
events.remedy_receipt: The decision orders a defined gross amount and deadline, but no worker-confirmed receipt or bank/payment record is public
events.durability_followup: The decision establishes long prior platform tenure and an ordered return route, but not post-order access, payment, recurrence, or later work
events.immediate_outcome: A formal reactivation and defined lost-earnings order converted a platform-access failure into a quantified remedy, while execution remained unobserved
events.protected_outcome: The order protected a route back to the platform and recognized a bounded income loss; actual cash recovery and durable earning capacity remain unknown
events.sacrificed_outcome: The worker lost platform access, income, and reputational security during the dispute and had to rely partly on other work
events.cost_risk_transfer: The platform's deactivation shifted income risk to the worker; the Commission shifted a quantified portion of the loss back to the platform while leaving payment execution to the order
events.later_outcome: The public decision ends at the reactivation and $6,073.23 order; later receipt, account activity, earnings, trust, switching, and exit are unknown
events.meaning_and_attribution: The Commission rejected a simple platform belief standard and required evidence of conduct and fair process; the worker's reported distress and reputational harm add a meaning/status dimension without a standardized trust measure
events.public_or_collective_response: Individual self-represented participation and formal adjudication are observed; no later collective or political action is reported
events.counterexample: A tribunal can quantify and order lost earnings while the public record still cannot show that the worker received the money or regained durable security
events.source_and_uncertainty: Primary Fair Work Commission decision [2025] FWC 3111, https://www.fwc.gov.au/documents/decisionssigned/pdf/2025fwc3111.pdf; the decision orders $6,073.23 gross less tax within 14 days but does not provide payment confirmation or later account evidence

arrows.from: long-term platform work and complaint-triggered deactivation
arrows.evidence: The decision records platform work from 2016, deactivation, a written response, discussion request, hearing evidence, and application
arrows.counterexample: A formal response route does not establish that other workers can safely or effectively use it
arrows.remaining_gap: Effort, delay, representation, household buffer, and alternative access

arrows.to: substitute work and quantified earnings calculation
arrows.evidence: The Commission used $951.03 average weekly earnings, $9,000 Baysec earnings, and an estimated $1,760 incremental Didi amount to calculate lost earnings
arrows.counterexample: Substitute earnings can reduce an ordered loss without showing equivalent work, control, stability, or household adequacy
arrows.remaining_gap: Work quality, hours, expenses, duration, household incidence, and equivalence

arrows.evidence: The decision orders same-terms reactivation within 7 days and $6,073.23 gross less tax within 14 days
arrows.counterexample: A defined order and deadline are not a verified payment or durable return
arrows.remaining_gap: Order compliance, payment channel, receipt, taxation, account restoration, and later work

arrows.to: cash recovery, durable work, trust, switching, or exit
arrows.evidence: The public decision does not report payment execution, later platform work, recurrence, trust, switching, or exit
arrows.counterexample: Quantified remedy can coexist with unobserved receipt and practical recovery
arrows.remaining_gap: Payment receipt, post-order account activity, earnings, household security, recurrence, trust, switching, and exit

boundary: This case advances the platform lane from formal reactivation to a quantified lost-earnings order and substitute-work accounting. It does not establish payment receipt, durable work, or recovery.
storage_boundary: No worker account, bank, trip, household, or platform-internal file is retained; only bounded public decision fields, dates, calculations, remedy terms, uncertainty, and open downstream arrows are represented.
